caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 347 of 2010
lawyer:
M.K. Rahman, Additional Attorney General, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record. ----- For the Petitioner 
TH Khan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Taufiq Hossain, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Respondent
parties:
The State ------ Petitioner.
VS
Md. Ariful Islam @ Arif ----- Respondent.
full_judgment:
S.K. Sinha J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 26th May, 2010 of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6566 of 2010 enlarging the accused-respondent Md. Ariful Islam @ Arif on bail in Motijheel P.S. Case No. 97 dated 22nd August, 2010 pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 2. Facts relevant for the disposal of this petition are that on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged with the Motijheel Police Station on 22nd August, 2004 over an occurrence alleged to have been committed on 21st August, 2004 at about 5.40 p.m. in front of the Central Office of Bangladesh Awami League, the Motijheel police registered the case and took it up for investigation. In the said incident 19 leaders and activists of Awami League succumbed to injuries and huge number of activists of the said political party sustained grievous injuries, some of them maimed. The police eventually submitted a charge sheet against 22 accused persons on 9th June, 2008. 

 3. The case record was eventually sent to the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka for trial and while the trial of the case was in progress on the prayer of the prosecution, the trial Court allowed further investigation of the case. The case is under investigation till now. 

 4. The accused-respondent was shown arrested in the case on 5th November, 2009 who unsuccessfully moved the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka and thereafter the High Court Division for bail. A Division Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties by the impugned order enlarged him on bail on the reasoning’s that "he has been in custody in connection with the case more than 6 months. Further investigation has not yet been concluded. No tangible materials have been placed before us for our appreciation that reasonable grounds exist to believe that he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life. We find no reason why the accused petitioner should be detained in custody simply for the purpose of further investigation in absence of materials placed before us showing that there are reasonable grounds for believing that he has been guilty of such offence. Heinousness of the offence which is shocking to human conscience by itself cannot be a ground for refusal of bail nor there is reason to refuse bail of an accused on a mere submission that he will jeopardize investigation if he is so enlarged". 

 5. We have heard the learned Additional Attorney General and perused the materials on record. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record exercised its discretion in favour admitting bail to the accused respondent with clear findings that there are no reasonable grounds for believing that the accused-respondent has committed a non-bailable offences, but that there are sufficient grounds for further inquiry into his guilt and pending such inquiry, he should be released on bail. Since the High Court Division has exercised its discretionary power in the matter of granting bail, this Court normally does not interfere with such power except in exceptional cases where such interference is called for in the interest of justice. Learned Additional Attorney General has failed to make out such a case. We find no merit in this petition.
